lutra-ledger.description: A high-performance, offline-first desktop application for generating complex PDF reports from client data, built with Rust, Tauri, and Svelte.
content: # Overview

Lutra Ledger is a fast, offline-first desktop application that helps UAB Lutra instantly turn client and service data into clean, professional PDF reports. Because it runs entirely on the user's machine, it is incredibly fast and keeps sensitive client data completely private. The app pairs a smooth web frontend with a powerful, secure Rust backend.
## Key Features
- **Custom Document Generation**: Automatically creates official corporate PDFs tailored for UAB Lutra, including invoices, orders, and receipts.

- **Smart Placeholders & Manual Editing**: Speeds up workflows by allowing to auto-filling forms with saved customer and service details, while still giving users full freedom to manually edit or overwrite any field for document-specific adjustments.
- **Live Document Preview**: Features a on-screen preview so users can review the layout, text, and structure of each document in real time before generating it.
- **Flexible File Saving**: Saves PDF files instantly upon clicking generate, allowing users to customize the file names and choose exactly which folder location to save them to.
- **Data Management Dashboards**: Built-in CRUD pages let users easily view, create, update, and delete customers, customer vehicles, services and generated historical invoices.
## How the App Communicates

- **Frontend to Backend (IPC)**: When a user clicks a button or inputs data in the Svelte frontend, the app uses Tauri commands (*tauri::command*) to send that data over to the Rust backend. The data is safely translated from TypeScript JSON into strict Rust formats.

- **Safe Multi-tasking**: The Rust backend uses Tauri’s managed state paired with a *Tokio* asynchronous runtime to handle database queries and file saving concurrently. This ensures complex background tasks run smoothly across threads without blocking the user interface or risking data corruption.
## Data & Local Storage

- **Local SQLite Database**: All core records, like clients, their vehicle information, services, and invoice histories, are saved locally in an embedded SQLite database. It uses Diesel ORM, which catches database query typos at compile time before the app is even built.

- **Automatic Setup & Updates**: Users don't need to configure a database. When the app starts up, it automatically uses *diesel_migrations* to check the local database file, create tables, or update the database structure silently in the background.

- **Saving App Settings**: While heavy data goes into SQLite, simple things like user preferences and app settings are handled differently. They are quietly saved as lightweight *.json* files in the user's system folder so their preferences carry over every time they open the app.
## PDF Generation Engine

- **Fast PDF Compiling**: Instead of using heavy browser engines to print a webpage or simply filling out pre-existing template PDFs, the application builds every document entirely from scratch using the native Rust *genpdf* library. The backend constructs the layout, text flows, and tables dynamically in memory based on the exact user data provided.

- **Instant Saving**: Once the backend generates the PDF, it instantly writes it to the computer's hard drive using Rust’s fast file system tools, giving the user a highly compressed, crisp document ready to print.
## Technical Stack
- **Frontend**: *Svelte* and *TypeScript* for a fast, reactive UI, styled cleanly with *Tailwind CSS*.
- **Desktop Frame**: *Tauri*, which keeps the app incredibly lightweight (under 50MB of RAM) by using the computer's built-in web viewer instead of a heavy Chromium window.
- **Backend**: *Rust* for native execution speed, safety, and excellent performance.
- **Database**: *SQLite* paired with *Diesel ORM* for safe, self-contained data storage.

rhythmic.description: A cross-platform music management tool to organize, version, and synchronize playlists between Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud.
content: # Overview

Rhythmic combines Spotify, SoundCloud, and YouTube into a single, convenient dashboard. Instead of jumping between different apps, you can manage, sync, and back up all your music in one place. A custom-built synchronization engine ensures these platforms connect seamlessly.
## Key Features

- **Playlist Transferring**: Seamlessly migrate entire music libraries across platforms, such as moving a playlist from YouTube to Spotify, or cloning data from one YouTube account directly to another.

- **Automated Parent-Child Sync**: Link multiple playlists together across different platforms by assigning parent and child relationships. Changes sync automatically every *n* hours, or can be triggered manually with an instant sync button.
- **Smart Duplication Cleanup**: Scans individual playlists to instantly identify duplicate tracks, giving users a clear interface to review and delete them in bulk.

- **Flexible Playlist Splitting**: Break oversized music libraries into smaller, highly organized segments based on specific rules, including splitting by specific artist, dividing perfectly in half, or grouping by a custom *n* number of tracks.
- **All-in-One Creation & Search**: Create, edit, and delete playlists. Users can search for tracks across multiple music streaming platforms simultaneously without ever leaving the application.

- **Version Control**: Keeps a running history of your music libraries like Git. The system automatically takes background snapshots every *x* hours and instantly records a new version whenever a change is made through the website, allowing users to view diffs and revert accidental deletions.
## How the Sync & Song Matching Works

- **The Platform-Mapping Engine**: When you transfer a playlist, the app fetches raw data from the source API (like Spotify), normalizes the track names, artists, and durations into a unified format, and then searches for matches on the target platform (like YouTube). All of this mapping logic was custom-built from scratch.

- **Fuzzy Text Matching (Jaro-Winkler)**: Song titles and artist names rarely match perfectly across different platforms due to typos, 'Remix' tags, or extra spaces. To fix this, the app uses the *Jaro-Winkler algorithm*. This formula compares two text strings and scores their similarity from 0 to 1, giving extra weight to strings that start with the same characters. If a search result scores above a certain threshold (e.g., 0.85), the app automatically pairs them up, ensuring highly accurate playlist transfers without forcing the user to fix every track manually.
## System Architecture & Live Data Flows

- **Real-Time Progress (SignalR WebSockets)**: Transferring hundreds of songs takes time. Instead of making the user guess what's happening, the backend uses *SignalR* to establish a live WebSocket connection with the React frontend. As the backend processes the playlist, it pushes instant updates to the UI, showing the user exactly which song is being matched and transferred in real time.

- **Smart Provider Factories**: To handle login and API calls cleanly, the backend uses a Factory Pattern. For example, when a user hits the `oauth/{provider}` endpoint, a factory service dynamically checks the 'provider' parameter. It then instantiates and returns the exact service client needed, whether that is Google, Spotify, or SoundCloud. This keeps the controllers completely decoupled from specific API logics.

- **Clean Architecture**: The * .NET 9* backend is strictly split into four distinct layers: *Domain* (core logic and music models), *Application* (use cases and business rules), *Infrastructure* (external API clients and database contexts), and *API* (controllers and HTTP endpoints). This separation keeps the codebase easy to maintain, test, and scale.
## Data & Local Storage

- **Playlist Version Control**: The database doesn't just store your current playlists; it tracks changes over time like Git. If you accidentally delete a song on Spotify, you can look at your playlist history in Rhythmic and revert it to an older version.

- **Relational Metadata Storage**: The app uses *MySQL* paired with *Entity Framework Core* to handle complex relationships, mapping a single user profile to multiple third-party OAuth sessions, playlist snapshots, and historical track logs.
## Technical Stack
- **Frontend**: *React* and *TypeScript* for a smooth, single-page application experience.
- **Backend Core**: *.NET 9* and *ASP.NET Core Web API* organized via Clean Architecture.
- **Real-Time Layer**: *SignalR* for pushing live WebSocket updates to the client.
- **Database Engine**: *MySQL* managed seamlessly with *Entity Framework Core*.

blaze-website.description: A web platform for Blaze.lt, featuring real-time Minecraft server synchronization and automated payment processing.
content: # Overview

Blaze.lt is a sophisticated gaming community portal designed to bridge the gap between web-based services and live Minecraft game data. By creating a unified dashboard, the platform allows players to track live server stats, manage their accounts, and process transactions—all from a single, responsive interface.
## Key Features

- **Minecraft Live-Sync**: Features deep integration with Minecraft game servers. The web platform pulls live player counts, rank information, and server status updates in real time, ensuring players always have the latest information.

- **Automated Payment Pipeline**: Integrated directly with *Paysera* to handle secure service purchases and donations. The system automatically processes payments and triggers in-game commands to deliver digital rewards to the player instantly.

- **Reactivity-First UI**: Built to be fast and dynamic. Using *Svelte’s* core reactivity, the dashboard updates player statistics and server status on the fly without ever needing a manual page refresh.
## System Architecture

- **Game-Web Bridge**: The application maintains high data consistency by utilizing shared *MySQL* database schemas and secure HTTPS API endpoints, allowing the game server and the website to communicate seamlessly.

- **Type-Safe Database Layer**: To prevent data-related bugs, the backend uses *Drizzle ORM*. This provides full type-safety for all queries against the *MySQL* database, ensuring that player data, transaction logs, and server stats are always handled with strict structural integrity.
## Technical Stack
- **Frontend**: *Svelte* and *TypeScript* for a reactive, lightning-fast single-page application experience.
- **Styling**: *Tailwind CSS* used to craft a custom, gaming-centric aesthetic that is fully responsive and accessible.
- **Database & Backend**: *MySQL* paired with *Drizzle ORM* for reliable, type-safe data handling and complex transaction processing.

timitis.description: A Project Management System with tailored portals for clients, employees, and managers to track tasks and log hours.
content: # Overview

Developed during a professional internship, Timitis is a project management tool designed to bridge the gap between internal development teams and external clients. Instead of using separate tools for emails, task boards, and client updates, this system centralizes everything. It uses a strict modular layout so that multiple client companies can use the app without ever seeing each other's data.
## Key Features
- **Four-Tier Access Control**: Features separate dashboards for Admins, Managers, Employees, and Clients, ensuring everyone sees exactly the data they need and nothing else.

- **Isolated Project Visibility**: Projects are assigned to specific clients and employees. Regular users can only see their own assigned work, while Managers and Admins keep a bird's-eye view of everything.

- **Kanban Boards & Time Logs**: Every project includes an interactive Kanban board where tasks are assigned to developers. Employees can log the exact hours spent working on each task to keep progress transparent.
- **Live Email Notifications**: An automated email system keeps everyone in the loop by sending out direct notifications to employees and clients whenever project statuses change or updates occur.
- **Dynamic Media Uploads**: Built to support more than text—users can upload images and videos directly to tasks, which are stored securely on the local server filesystem.
## How the App Works

- **Modular Clean Architecture**: The *Spring Boot* backend follows Clean Architecture principles, splitting the code into *API*, *Application*, *Domain*, and *Infrastructure* layers. On top of that, the app is organized into functional modules like a *core module* for shared code and a *clients module* for client-specific rules. This keeps the codebase highly organized and easy to expand.

- **Secure Login (JWT)**: When a user logs in from the React frontend, the backend generates a secure *JWT (JSON Web Token)*. The frontend stores this token and attaches it to future requests, allowing the backend to immediately verify who the user is and what role they have without re-checking credentials every time.

- **Smart Database Queries**: The app uses *Spring Data JPA* to communicate with a *MySQL* database. This allows the system to easily handle complex relationships - like linking a single project to multiple tasks, a specific client company, a team of employees - using safe, fast, and pre-built Java methods.

- **Decoupled Settings**: System configuration options are saved directly in the database rather than being hardcoded into configuration files. This means administrators can change runtime settings like file upload size limits or email server keys directly through the UI without restarting the server.
## Technical Stack
- **Frontend**: *React* and *TypeScript* for a reliable, type-safe user interface, using *Axios* to handle API requests and send security tokens.
- **Backend Engine**: *Spring Boot* organized into a clean, modular structure for predictable backend performance.
- **Data & Media Storage**: *MySQL* managed via *Spring Data JPA* for structural records, combined with local server filesystem storage for uploaded images and videos.

worsetagram.description: A functional Instagram-inspired Android application developed to explore Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and modern mobile architecture.
content: # Overview

Worsetagram is a social media application designed to replicate the core mechanics of Instagram. Built from the ground up as a learning project, it handles everything from media upload pipelines to live chat. The goal of the project was to master modern Android development standards, specifically focusing on how to manage asynchronous data flows and reactive user interfaces.
## Key Features

- **Content Creation & Interactive Feed**: Users can upload images from their device gallery, write captions, and publish them to a global feed where other users can like and comment on posts in real time.
- **Social Follow System**: Includes a fully functional following system. Users can visit profiles, follow or unfollow accounts, and see their follower and following counts update instantly.
- **Real-Time Direct Messaging**: Features a private chat interface where users can search for other accounts and send instant, direct messages that update without needing to refresh the screen.
- **Profile Customization**: Dedicated user spaces displaying bio information, follower metrics, and a clean grid layout of all their historical image posts.
## How the App Works

- **Clean Architecture & Layers**: The app code is strictly organized into three distinct layers: *UI* (handling what the user sees), *Domain* (holding the core business logic and use cases), and *Data* (managing API and database connections). This separation makes the code highly modular, readable, and easy to unit test.

- **Declarative UI**: The entire user interface is built using *Jetpack Compose*. Instead of old-school XML layouts, the UI is written entirely in Kotlin, automatically updating whenever the underlying data state changes for a completely smooth user experience.

- **Real-Time Serverless Backend**: The app relies heavily on the *Firebase* ecosystem. It uses *Firebase Auth* to handle secure user sign-ups and logins, *Cloud Firestore* as a real-time database to sync messages, comments, and follows instantly, and *Firebase Storage* to host uploaded post images.

- **Clean Dependency Management**: To keep the codebase organized, *Dagger-Hilt* handles dependency injection. It automatically passes database instances and repositories into ViewModels, preventing messy setup code and keeping components loosely coupled.
## Technical Stack
- **Frontend & Design**: *Jetpack Compose* for native Android UI development, styled with modern Material Design principles.
- **Language & Quality**: Written in *Kotlin*, with strict code formatting automatically enforced by *ktfmt* to match Google's official styling standards.
- **Backend Ecosystem**: *Firebase* (Auth, Firestore, and Storage) for a completely serverless, reactive data pipeline.

purrislav.description: A Discord bot built in Rust that automates community engagement through birthday tracking and dynamic role management.
content: # Overview
Purrislav is a lightweight utility bot designed for long-term stability and low-footprint hosting on a VPS.
## Core Features
- **Birthday System**: Server members can register their birthdays; the bot performs a daily automated check to send reminders to a designated channel.
- **Color Roles**: Provides an intuitive interface for users to create and manage custom colored roles within the server.
- **Slash Commands**: Fully integrated with the modern Discord API for a seamless user experience.
## Technical Stack
- Developed using **Rust** and the **Poise** framework for high concurrency and type safety.
- Data persistence handled by **SQLite**, providing a self-contained and portable database solution.
- Utilizes **Diesel ORM** for robust database migrations and compile-time checked queries.

blackjack.description: A browser-based implementation of the classic casino card game, featuring Glassmorphism UI and optimized for smooth web play.
content: # Overview
A pure JavaScript game that simulates a high-stakes Blackjack experience directly in your browser without the need for external libraries.
## Game Mechanics
- **Scoring Logic**: Cards 2-10 hold face value, J/Q/K are worth 10, and Aces are dynamically valued at 11.
- **Objective**: Compete against a virtual dealer to reach a total as close to 21 as possible without 'busting'.
- **Dealer AI**: Includes an automated dealer behavior loop for a consistent single-player challenge.
## Highlights
- **Glassmorphism Design**: Minimalist, frosted-glass interface built with modern CSS properties.
- **Vanilla Implementation**: Developed using only **HTML5**, **CSS3**, and **ES6+ JavaScript**, ensuring fast load times and zero dependencies.

sortvisualizer.description: A desktop-based visualization tool built with WinForms to demonstrate the mechanics and efficiency of various sorting algorithms.
content: # Overview
SortVisualizer provides a graphical representation of how data moves during sorting, helping to understand the time complexity and logic behind different algorithms.
## Supported Algorithms
- **Divide & Conquer**: Merge Sort, Quick Sort, and Heap Sort.
- **Classic Sorts**: Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, and Insertion Sort.
- **Unique Sorts**: Gnome Sort and Pancake Sort.
## Key Features
- **Execution Timing**: Built-in timers to compare the real-world performance of each algorithm side-by-side.
- **Step-by-Step Rendering**: Watch the array transform in real-time as the algorithms swap and compare elements.
- **Native Performance**: Built entirely in **C#** using the **Windows Forms** (WinForms) framework for a lightweight desktop experience.
